narrative: The model estimated a 94% chance that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt, so your application was denied on that basis. This is a strong risk estimate, not a guarantee, but it means the decision was driven mainly by the model’s view of your academic preparation. The strongest factor was your third-year class standing: you were in the first decile, while accepted students averaged near the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward failure more than any other item. Your first-year class standing was the next strongest factor; it also placed you in the first decile against an accepted-student average near the sixth, reinforcing the same concern. Your undergraduate GPA was the third most influential factor, but it actually worked in your favor: at 3.10 it was only slightly below the accepted average of 3.23 and pushed toward passing, though it could not outweigh the class-standing signals. To move forward, ask admissions what specific evidence would address their bar-readiness concern, work with an academic advisor on a concrete preparation plan, consider whether retaking the LSAT or strengthening your academic record is appropriate, and reapply once you can show measurable improvement.
